1	# Data Lineage Trust Platform
2	
3	Backend service for managing datasets, their immutable schema versions and
4	field-level lineage between schema versions. All metadata is persisted in a
5	SQLite database, so data created before a restart remains queryable afterwards.
6	
7	## Requirements
8	
9	- Python 3.12+
10	
11	## Install and test
12	
13	```bash
14	python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'
15	python -m pytest
16	```
17	
18	## Start
19	
20	```bash
21	python -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
22	```
23	
24	The SQLite database is stored at `data/lineage.db` by default. Override the
25	location with the `DATA_LINEAGE_DB` environment variable.
26	
27	## Public API
28	
29	All endpoints return JSON. Error responses use the stable shape
30	`{"error": "<code>", "detail": "<message>"}` and never expose SQL or stack
31	traces.
32	
33	### Health
34	
35	- `GET /health` returns `{"status":"ok"}` when the service is ready.
36	
37	### Datasets
38	
39	- `POST /datasets` — create a dataset. Body: `{"name": "orders", "description": "optional"}`.
40	  Returns `201` with `id`, `name`, `description`, `created_at`. Empty name →
41	  `422`; duplicate name → `409`.
42	- `GET /datasets` — list all datasets.
43	
44	### Schema versions (immutable, numbered from 1 per dataset)
45	
46	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions` — create the next schema version. Body:
47	  `{"fields": [{"name": "id", "type": "integer", "nullable": false}]}`.
48	  Field list must be non-empty, field `name`/`type`/`nullable` are required and
49	  field names must be unique within the version. Unknown dataset → `404`;
50	  invalid fields → `422` (nothing is written).
51	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions` — list all versions of a dataset with
52	  their fields.
53	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}` — read one version with its
54	  fields. Unknown dataset/version → `404`.
55	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{base_version}/compatibility/{target_version}` —
56	  read-only breaking-change check of the target version against the base
57	  version, computed fresh from the persisted field definitions on every read
58	  (nothing is written; field order is not a difference). The endpoint takes no
59	  request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version →
60	  `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the version diff. The JSON
61	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
62	  trailing newline) with top-level keys `base_version`, `target_version`,
63	  `breaking_changes` and `breaking_change_count`. A breaking change is exactly
64	  one of: the target removed a base field (`removed`), changed a field's type
65	  (`type_changed`) or tightened a nullable field to not nullable
66	  (`nullable_tightened`); added fields and nullable loosening are not
67	  breaking. Each entry has `field`, `kind`, `before` (base definition) and
68	  `after` (target definition, `null` for a removed field), entries are sorted
69	  by field name ascending and `breaking_change_count` equals the number of
70	  entries. Comparing a version with itself returns an empty list and a zero
71	  count. The verdict is advisory for release decisions only: it runs no
72	  migration or rollback.
73	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{base_version}/compatibility/{target_version}/impact` —
74	  read-only companion of the compatibility check: the same top-level keys
75	  (`base_version`, `target_version`, `breaking_changes`,
76	  `breaking_change_count`) and the same breaking entries, each entry carrying
77	  one extra key `impacted` after `after`. `impacted` lists every field
78	  directly or indirectly downstream of the broken field along the lineage
79	  mappings, starting from the base version's same-named field and — when the
80	  field still exists in the target version — also from the target version's
81	  field. Each item is `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`; the set is
82	  deduplicated, never contains a start field itself (cycles terminate) and is
83	  sorted by dataset, version and field ascending. A field with no downstream
84	  yields an empty list. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
85	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404` with the same
86	  404-before-422 precedence as the compatibility check, and the JSON document
87	  is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
88	  newline). The read is fully side-effect free: version definitions, lineage
89	  mappings and the impact cache are never written.
90	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/evolution-summary` — read-only whole-dataset
91	  summary of adjacent-version breaking changes and their downstream impact,
92	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version
93	  definitions, lineage mappings and the impact cache are never touched).
94	  Quality and privacy state play no role. The path carries only the dataset
95	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters (`422`); an unknown
96	  dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
97	  compatibility reads. A dataset with fewer than two versions returns `200`
98	  with an empty `pairs` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
99	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
100	  trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`, `pairs` and `totals`.
101	  `pairs` is ordered by base version number ascending and lists every
102	  adjacent version pair, including pairs without breaking changes; each entry
103	  has exactly `base_version`, `target_version`, `breaking_count`,
104	  `impacted_count` and `impacted_datasets` in that order. `breaking_count` is
105	  the number of breaking entries of the pair, judged exactly as in the
106	  pairwise compatibility impact response (`removed`, `type_changed` or
107	  `nullable_tightened`; several changes of one field collapse into a single
108	  entry). The pair's impacted set is the union of every breaking entry's
109	  downstream fields — same start-field rule as the pairwise impact response,
110	  merged and deduplicated, never containing a start field itself (cycles
111	  terminate) — `impacted_count` is its size and `impacted_datasets` lists the
112	  distinct dataset names appearing in it, sorted ascending. `totals` has
113	  exactly `pair_count` (the number of pairs), `breaking_count` and
114	  `impacted_count`, each the sum of the per-pair values over the whole
115	  dataset.
116	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/fields/{field}/trajectory` — read-only
117	  cross-version trajectory of one named field of the dataset, computed fresh
118	  on every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version definitions,
119	  lineage mappings and the impact cache are never touched). Only the
120	  persisted version field definitions and lineage mappings are read; quality,
121	  privacy, snapshot and processing-task state play no role. The path carries
122	  the dataset name and the field name; the request takes no body and no query
123	  parameters (`422`); an unknown dataset → `404`, and a field that does not
124	  appear in any of the dataset's versions → `404`, both with the same
125	  404-before-422 precedence as the evolution summary. A dataset with fewer
126	  than two versions returns `200` with an empty `changes` array, never an
127	  error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact
128	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`,
129	  `field`, `entries` and `changes` in that order. `entries` lists every
130	  schema version of the dataset ordered by version number ascending; each
131	  entry has exactly `version` and `definition`, where `definition` is the
132	  field's persisted definition in that version (`type` and `nullable` only)
133	  or `null` — the key is never omitted — when the field does not exist
134	  there. `changes` lists one entry per adjacent version pair, ordered by
135	  base version ascending; each entry has exactly `base_version`,
136	  `target_version`, `status`, `impacted` and `impacted_datasets` in that
137	  order. `status` reuses the breaking-entry vocabulary of the compatibility
138	  check — `added` (the field appears on the target side), `removed` (it
139	  disappears on the target side), `type_changed`, `nullable_tightened` —
140	  extended with `nullable_loosened` (only the nullability relaxes) and
141	  `unchanged` (both definitions agree, including both absent); a field that
142	  both changes type and tightens nullability collapses into a single
143	  `type_changed` status. `impacted` lists every field directly or indirectly
144	  downstream of the tracked field for that pair along the lineage mappings,
145	  with the same start-field rule as the pairwise compatibility impact
146	  response (the base version's same-named field and, when it exists, the
147	  target version's); each item is `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`, the set
148	  is deduplicated, never contains a start field itself (cycles terminate),
149	  is sorted by dataset, version and field ascending and is empty when the
150	  field has no downstream. `impacted_datasets` lists the distinct dataset
151	  names appearing in `impacted`, sorted ascending.
152	
153	### Field-level lineage
154	
155	A lineage link maps one field of a target schema version to one field of a
156	schema version in a different (source) dataset.
157	
158	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — register a mapping.
159	  Body names both ends:
160	
161	  ```json
162	  {
163	    "target_dataset": "dm_orders",
164	    "target_version": 1,
165	    "target_field": "id",
166	    "source_dataset": "raw_orders",
167	    "source_version": 1,
168	    "source_field": "order_id"
169	  }
170	  ```
171	
172	  Target must match the path. Source and target datasets must differ and every
173	  referenced dataset/version/field must exist (`404` / `422` otherwise).
174	  Submitting the same complete mapping twice returns `409`.
175	- `DELETE /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — remove one
176	  registered mapping. Same address and same body shape as registration: the
177	  six locating fields name the complete mapping to delete and the body target
178	  must match the path. Every locating value readable in the request is
179	  resolved first, so an unknown dataset, version or field is a `404` ahead of
180	  every request-shape error; when all six values name existing resources but
181	  the mapping itself was never registered, the delete is likewise a `404`.
182	  An empty or whitespace body, invalid JSON, a non-object payload, missing or
183	  extra fields, wrongly typed values, blank names, any query parameter, a
184	  mapping whose source and target datasets coincide or whose body target
185	  disagrees with the path are all `422`. No rejection changes the lineage
186	  graph, the impact cache or any other metadata. A registered mapping is
187	  deleted atomically and returns `200` with the removed mapping in the
188	  registration response shape; concurrent deletes of the same mapping succeed
189	  exactly once (the loser gets `404` and changes nothing). The deletion is
190	  visible to every lineage read immediately and survives restarts; the cached
191	  impacts of the mapping's source field and of every field that can reach it
192	  are invalidated exactly as on registration, unrelated entries are kept.
193	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — return every target
194	  field (including fields without sources) together with its source references.
195	  Results are sorted by target field name, then source dataset name, source
196	  version and source field name.
197	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact?field=<field>` —
198	  return the downstream impact of one source field. The path and the `field`
199	  query parameter together name an existing field; the response is
200	  `{"source": {...}, "impacted": [...]}` where `impacted` lists every field
201	  reachable from the source along lineage mappings (direct and indirect), each
202	  entry being `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. Results are deduplicated,
203	  never contain the source itself (cycles terminate) and are sorted by dataset,
204	  version and field ascending. Unknown dataset/version/field → `404`; a
205	  missing, blank, invalid or repeated `field` parameter → `422` (a repeated
206	  `field` is judged before the field lookup, so it is always a `422`, never a
207	  field `404`).
208	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/cache-audit` —
209	  read-only consistency audit of the version's impact cache, appended one
210	  segment after the impact query address. The path dataset and version name
211	  the audit scope; every field of that version is checked against its current
212	  cache record and recomputed fresh from the committed lineage graph using
213	  exactly the impact-query semantics (downstream fields merged and
214	  deduplicated, the start field excluded, cycles terminating). Each entry is
215	  `{"field", "status"}` with `cached` (the stored record equals the
216	  recomputed result), `missing` (no cache record because the field's impact
217	  was never queried — a normal state, not an error) or `mismatch` (the stored
218	  record differs). Entries are sorted by field name ascending and the sort
219	  does not depend on database order. The JSON document is deterministic
220	  (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with
221	  top-level keys `dataset`, `version`, `entries` and `counts` in that order;
222	  `counts` gives `cached_count`, `missing_count` and `mismatch_count`, each
223	  equal to the number of entries with that status. The audit is computed on
224	  every read and never writes: no cache record is inserted, invalidated or
225	  repaired, so impact queries, impact paths and source paths behave exactly
226	  as before. The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters; any
227	  body bytes (whitespace-only included) or query parameter → `422`, and an
228	  unknown dataset or version → `404`, with `404` taking precedence over
229	  `422` as in the impact query.
230	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/cache-audit/repair`
231	  — controlled repair of the version's impact cache, appended one segment
232	  after the read-only audit address and accepting POST only. Every field of
233	  the version is recomputed against the committed lineage graph with the
234	  exact impact-query semantics: a field without a cache record gets one
235	  (`created`), a stored record that disagrees is rewritten (`updated`) and a
236	  matching record is left untouched (`unchanged`). Entries are sorted by
237	  field name ascending and the JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
238	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level
239	  keys `dataset`, `version`, `entries` and `counts` in that order; each
240	  entry has exactly `field` and `action`, and `counts` gives
241	  `created_count`, `updated_count` and `unchanged_count`. Written records
242	  are ordinary cache rows visible immediately to impact queries and
243	  surviving restarts; a subsequent audit reports every field as `cached`.
244	  The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters — any body
245	  bytes (whitespace-only included) or query parameter → `422`, an unknown
246	  dataset or version → `404` (with `404` taking precedence as in the audit),
247	  and concurrent repairs of the same version have a single winner, the
248	  loser receiving `409` and changing nothing. Every rejection writes
249	  nothing; lineage registrations and deletions, impact queries, path
250	  explanations, source-path reads and the read-only audit are unaffected.
251	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/cache-invalidations`
252	  — read-only invalidation trail of the version's impact cache, appended one
253	  segment after the impact query address and accepting GET only. Whenever a
254	  lineage mapping is successfully registered or deleted, every invalidated
255	  field that actually had a cache record (the mapping's source field and
256	  every field that can reach it) leaves one append-only record under its own
257	  dataset and version; cache invalidation triggered by schema version
258	  creation leaves no trail. Each entry has exactly `sequence`, `cause`,
259	  `field` and `created_at` in that order: `sequence` numbers the version's
260	  records from 1 in write order (continuous, never reused, even under
261	  concurrent registrations and deletions), `cause` is `registered` or
262	  `deleted` after the triggering mapping write and `created_at` is the
263	  timezone-bearing write time. Entries are sorted by sequence ascending and
264	  a version without records returns an empty `entries` array, never an
265	  error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact
266	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`,
267	  `version` and `entries` in that order. The trail is append-only and
268	  survives restarts; the read only reads persisted records and never writes,
269	  invalidates or repairs anything. The endpoint takes no request body and no
270	  query parameters; any body bytes (whitespace-only included) or query
271	  parameter → `422`, and an unknown dataset or version → `404`, with `404`
272	  taking precedence over `422` as in the impact query.
273	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact-paths?field=<field>` —
274	  read-only shortest-path explanation of the same impact, computed fresh on
275	  every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version definitions, lineage
276	  mappings and the impact cache are never touched). The path and the `field`
277	  query parameter together name an existing field. The JSON document is
278	  deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
279	  newline) with top-level keys `source`, `impacts`, `direct_count` and
280	  `indirect_count` in that order; `source` is the start field reference

286	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}` shape; `path_length` is the number of
287	  edges on the path (`1` for a direct downstream field, increasing for

291	  the fields farther away, and a field with no downstream returns an empty

297	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/source-paths?field=<field>` —

309	  entries are deduplicated, never contain the start field and are sorted by
310	  dataset, version and field ascending. An origin is a field whose mapping
311	  points (directly or transitively) at the start field. `path` is the
312	  shortest node sequence walking from the start field up to the origin,
313	  including both ends, and each node has the same

316	  Among several shortest paths, the lexicographically smallest node sequence
317	  (compared by dataset, version and field) is chosen; cycles terminate.
318	  `direct_count` counts origins at distance 1, `indirect_count` the origins

324	  taking precedence over every `422` except that a repeated `field` is judged

327	  reporting, for every schema version at once, how the version's fields are

339	  `source_dataset_count` of zero; that count counts the distinct source
340	  dataset names among the references, never the number of mappings.
341	  `mapping_count` equals the sum of the fields' source-reference counts and

344	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`,
345	  `versions` and `totals` in that order; `totals` gives `version_count`,
346	  `field_count`, `linked_field_count`, `unlinked_field_count` and
347	  `mapping_count`, each equal to the sum of the matching per-version values

351	  takes no request body and no query parameters; any body bytes
352	  (whitespace-only included) or query parameter → `422`, and an unknown
353	  dataset → `404`, with `404` taking precedence over the shape checks.
354	
355	  Impact results are cached persistently (they survive restarts) and every
356	  read reflects the currently committed lineage graph: creating a schema
357	  version invalidates the cache entries related to that dataset, and creating
358	  or deleting a lineage mapping invalidates the cached impacts of the
359	  mapping's source field and of every field that can reach it. Unrelated
360	  cache entries are preserved.

362	### Quality rules
363	
364	Quality rules validate rows against a schema version. Rules are version-scoped
365	and persisted (including their enabled state) across restarts.
366	
367	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — create a rule.
368	  Body: `{"name": "id required", "kind": "not_null", "params": {...}}`. Returns
369	  `201` with `id`, `name`, `kind`, `params`, `enabled`, `created_at`; `enabled`
370	  defaults to `true`. Rule names must be unique within a version (`409` on
371	  conflict). Referenced dataset/version/field must exist (`404`); other invalid
372	  input returns `422` and nothing is written. Supported kinds:
373	  - `not_null` — params `{"field": "<existing field>"}`.
374	  - `numeric_range` — params `{"field": "<existing field>", "min": <finite
375	    number>, "max": <finite number>}` with `min <= max`.
376	  - `unique` — params `{"fields": ["<existing field>", ...]}`: a non-empty list
377	    of distinct, existing field names.
378	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — list rules
379	  sorted by `id` ascending.
380	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/{rule_id}` —
381	  enable or disable a rule. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
382	  the updated rule. Unknown rule/dataset/version → `404`.
383	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluate` —
384	  evaluate rows. Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}`. Only enabled rules run.
385	  Returns `{"dataset", "version", "results"}` with results sorted by `rule_id`;
386	  each result has `rule_id`, `name`, `passed` and `violations` (0-based row
387	  indices in ascending order).
388	  - `not_null` fails on missing or `null` values.
389	  - `numeric_range` fails on missing, `null`, non-numeric, boolean or
390	    out-of-range values (boundaries included).
391	  - `unique` compares the tuple of `fields` values per row; a missing field
392	    counts as `null`, and every row taking part in a duplicate group is a
393	    violation.
394	  - With an empty `rows` list every rule passes.
395	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations` —
396	  list the persisted evaluation history of the version, ordered by `sequence`
397	  (occurrence order). Every successful evaluation appends one immutable
398	  summary (`sequence`, `dataset`, `version`, `row_count`,
399	  `violation_row_count` — the number of distinct submitted rows violating at
400	  least one rule — `results` and `created_at`); rejected or failed
401	  evaluations leave no record, and an empty `rows` submission is recorded
402	  with zero violations. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
403	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
404	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/at?timestamp=...`
405	  — read-only point-in-time single-record look-back, appended one segment
406	  after the evaluation history address and accepting GET only. `timestamp`
407	  must be a timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time (an offset or trailing `Z`);
408	  only evaluation summaries written at or before it form the look-back
409	  window, and the returned summary is the window's highest-sequence record
410	  in exactly the single-record shape of the history (`sequence`, `dataset`,
411	  `version`, `row_count`, `violation_row_count`, `results`, `created_at`).
412	  A window with no recorded evaluation is a normal response, not an error:
413	  the same key set is still returned with `sequence`, `row_count`,
414	  `violation_row_count` and `created_at` set to null (keys are never
415	  omitted) and `results` an empty list. Only persisted evaluation summaries
416	  are read: rules are never re-run, history summaries are never rewritten,
417	  nothing is cached or written, and the window grows naturally as new
418	  evaluations are persisted, so the same data yields the same document byte
419	  for byte across process restarts, and the ordering of rule results never
420	  depends on database natural order. The JSON document is deterministic
421	  (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline). The
422	  path dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body
423	  bytes (whitespace-only included), a missing, repeated, unparseable or
424	  timezone-less `timestamp`, or any other query parameter are a `422` that
425	  writes nothing. Errors keep the stable `{"error", "detail"}` shape without
426	  exposing SQL, stack traces or internal objects; the evaluation history,
427	  the pairwise and point-in-time diffs and every other endpoint are
428	  unchanged.
429	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/diff`
430	  — read-only diff between the two most recent recorded evaluations
431	  (`from_sequence` → `to_sequence`). `added_violation_rows` /
432	  `removed_violation_rows` are the 0-based row indices that started or
433	  stopped violating any rule, and each entry of `rules` carries the rule's
434	  `before`/`after` side (`violation_count` and `violations`), the per-rule
435	  `added_violations` / `removed_violations` and the numeric
436	  `violation_count_delta` (negative, zero or positive). A rule missing from
437	  one side (disabled or created between the two evaluations) has a `null`
438	  side and `null` row-level diff fields. With fewer than two recorded
439	  evaluations the response is an explicit empty result (null sequences,
440	  empty lists), not an error. The path dataset/version resolves first
441	  (`404`); afterwards any request body bytes (whitespace-only included) or
442	  any query parameter are a `422` that writes nothing.
443	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/diff/at?timestamp=...`
444	  — read-only point-in-time companion of the evaluation diff, appended one
445	  segment after the pairwise diff address and accepting GET only.
446	  `timestamp` must be a timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time (an offset or
447	  trailing `Z`); only evaluation summaries written at or before it count as
448	  the look-back window, and the two that participate are the window's
449	  highest-sequence pair — the newest is `to`, its predecessor `from`. The
450	  comparison is exactly the pairwise diff's: `added_violation_rows` /
451	  `removed_violation_rows` are the 0-based row indices that started or
452	  stopped violating any rule, and each `rules` entry carries the rule's
453	  `before`/`after` side (`violation_count` and `violations`), the per-rule
454	  `added_violations` / `removed_violations` and the numeric
455	  `violation_count_delta`. A rule missing from one side (disabled or created
456	  between the two evaluations) has a `null` side and `null` row-level diff
457	  fields — the key is never omitted. A window with fewer than two recorded
458	  evaluations returns the same explicit empty result as the pairwise diff
459	  (null sequences, empty lists), not an error. Only persisted evaluation
460	  summaries are read: rules are never re-run, history summaries are never
461	  rewritten, nothing is cached or written, and the window grows naturally as
462	  new evaluations are persisted, so the same data yields the same document
463	  byte for byte across process restarts. The JSON document is deterministic
464	  (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline). The
465	  path dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body
466	  bytes (whitespace-only included), a missing, repeated, unparseable or
467	  timezone-less `timestamp`, or any other query parameter are a `422` that
468	  writes nothing. Errors keep the stable `{"error", "detail"}` shape without
469	  exposing SQL, stack traces or internal objects; the evaluation history,
470	  the pairwise diff and every other endpoint are unchanged.
471	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/trend`
472	  — read-only trend summary, appended one segment after the evaluation
473	  history address and accepting GET only. The caller sends no request body
474	  and no query parameter. The summary is computed fresh from the persisted
475	  evaluation history on every read: rules are never re-run, history
476	  summaries are never rewritten, nothing is cached or written, and the same
477	  history yields the same document byte for byte across process restarts,
478	  with every ordering explicit rather than dependent on database natural
479	  order.
480	  - `evaluations` lists one entry per evaluation ordered by ascending
481	    `sequence`, each carrying the history summary's `created_at` (write
482	    time), `row_count` (submitted rows) and `violation_row_count`, plus
483	    `violation_row_count_delta` — the change in violation row count against
484	    the previous evaluation; on the first evaluation it is `null` and the
485	    key is never omitted.
486	  - `rules` gives one row per rule that appears in the history, sorted by
487	    rule id ascending, including rules that have since been disabled and
488	    rules that never recorded a violation. Each row carries `rule_id` and
489	    `name`, the cumulative `violation_row_count` (summed over evaluations),
490	    the `violating_evaluation_count`, and `first_violation_sequence` /
491	    `last_violation_sequence` — the sequences of the rule's first and last
492	    violating evaluation, both `null` (never omitted) when the rule never
493	    violated; its counts are zero in that case.
494	  - `totals` reports the whole-version `evaluation_count`, the
495	    `violation_row_count` total (the sum of the per-evaluation counts) and
496	    the `rule_count` of distinct rules the history involves. An empty
497	    history is an explicit empty result (empty `evaluations` and `rules`,
498	    all-zero totals), returned normally rather than as an error.
499	  - The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact
500	    whitespace, lowercase booleans, exactly one trailing newline). The path
501	    dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body
502	    bytes (whitespace-only included) or any query parameter are a `422`
503	    that writes nothing. Errors keep the stable `{"error", "detail"}`
504	    shape without exposing SQL, stack traces or internal objects; the
505	    evaluation history, the pairwise and point-in-time diffs, anomaly
506	    detection and every other endpoint are unchanged.

508	### Quality anomaly detection
509	
510	Anomaly detection runs over the persisted evaluation history of a schema
511	version. A version carries at most one detection config; scans append
512	immutable anomaly records that persist across restarts.
513	
514	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
515	  — register the version's detection config. The body contains exactly three
516	  integers: `consecutive_worsening_steps` (at least `2`),
517	  `violation_row_limit` and `rule_violation_limit` (both non-negative).
518	  Returns `201` with the config (`id`, `dataset`, `version`, the three
519	  thresholds, `created_at`). A second config for the same version returns
520	  `409`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing, extra, non-integer or
521	  out-of-range fields → `422` and nothing is written.
522	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
523	  — return the registered config (`404` when none exists). The endpoint takes
524	  no request body and no query parameters (`422`).
525	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/scan`
526	  — run one detection pass over the persisted evaluation history and return
527	  the anomaly records this scan newly added (ordered by `id`); they are
528	  persisted in the same transaction. Scanning without a registered config
529	  returns `409`; an empty history is a successful scan that writes nothing.
530	  The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`). Each
531	  record has `id`, `kind`, `sequence` (the history sequence it points to),
532	  `rule_id`, `violation_count` and `created_at`; `kind` is one of:
533	  - `row_limit` — the evaluation's `violation_row_count` exceeds
534	    `violation_row_limit` (`rule_id` is `null`).
535	  - `rule_limit` — one rule's violation count in the evaluation exceeds
536	    `rule_violation_limit`; `rule_id` carries the rule's id.
537	  - `trend` — the violation row counts of adjacent evaluations strictly
538	    increase and the consecutive increase count at the tail of the history
539	    reaches `consecutive_worsening_steps`; the record points to the final
540	    evaluation of the increasing sequence (`rule_id` is `null`). A shorter
541	    run or any decline produces no trend record.
542	
543	  A record with the same kind, history sequence and rule id is never
544	  duplicated: repeated scans only persist and return newly appearing
545	  anomalies, and concurrent scans store each anomaly exactly once with
546	  contiguous ids.
547	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/anomalies`
548	  — list every anomaly record of the version sorted by `id` ascending (empty
549	  when there are none, never an error). Same `404`/`422` rules as the scan
550	  endpoint; nothing is written.

552	### Quality gate
553	
554	The quality gate is the release-readiness verdict of a schema version. It is
555	computed fresh from the persisted records on every read — nothing is cached,
556	re-run or written, and the rule definitions are never consulted (violations
557	recorded for rules since disabled still count).
558	
559	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/gate` — return the
560	  verdict as a deterministic JSON document (fixed key order, compact
561	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
562	  `{"dataset", "version", "verdict", "reasons", "counts"}`.
563	  - `verdict` is one of:
564	    - `pass` — the latest recorded evaluation passed every rule and no
565	      anomaly record exists; a zero-violation evaluation left by an empty
566	      `rows` submission is a valid basis.
567	    - `undetermined` — no evaluation was ever recorded; `reasons` is empty
568	      and the read succeeds (never an error).
569	    - `fail` — the latest recorded evaluation still has violating rows, or
570	      the version carries any anomaly record.
571	  - `reasons` lists every factor that lowers the verdict, sorted by `kind`,
572	    `sequence` and `rule_id` (null ids first), all ascending. Each reason has
573	    `kind`, `sequence`, `rule_id` and `violation_count` (a missing rule id is
574	    `null`, never omitted). Every rule with violations in the latest
575	    evaluation contributes one `violation` reason with its violation row
576	    count; every persisted anomaly record contributes one reason of its own
577	    kind (`row_limit`, `rule_limit` or `trend`). A rule that appears in both
578	    yields two reasons — they are never merged or deduplicated.
579	  - `counts` reports how many persisted records the verdict examined:
580	    `evaluations`, `anomalies` and `reasons` (the length of the reason list).
581	  - The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters: any body
582	    bytes — including whitespace-only ones — or any query parameter are a
583	    `422`, checked after the path dataset/version resolves (`404` first).
584	    Nothing is written on any rejection.
585	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/gate/at?timestamp=...`
586	  — the same verdict as it stood at a requested instant. `timestamp` must be
587	  a timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time; only evaluations and anomaly records
588	  written at or before it count, and the latest evaluation of that window is
589	  the one with the highest sequence inside it. The response is the same
590	  deterministic document as the bare gate (`dataset`, `version`, `verdict`,
591	  `reasons`, `counts`, one trailing newline), with the counts covering only
592	  the records inside the window. A window without any evaluation is
593	  `undetermined` with an empty reason list — a normal response, never an
594	  error. The endpoint accepts GET only and is strictly read-only. The path
595	  dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body bytes
596	  (whitespace-only included), a missing, repeated, unparseable or
597	  timezone-less `timestamp`, or any other query parameter are a `422` that
598	  writes nothing.
599	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/quality-gate-export` — read-only cross-version
600	  export of the dataset's whole quality gate state, computed fresh on every
601	  read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or deleted, and no
602	  evaluation, anomaly record or gate verdict is touched). The path carries
603	  only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no query parameters —
604	  any body bytes, including a purely whitespace or single-space body, or any
605	  query parameter → `422`; an unknown dataset → `404`, checked before the
606	  request shape, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the compliance
607	  exports. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an empty
608	  `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON document is
609	  deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
610	  newline):
611	
612	  ```json
613	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"verdict":"fail","reason_count":1,"violation_row_count":2},{"version":2,"verdict":"undetermined","reason_count":0,"violation_row_count":null}],"totals":{"version_count":2,"failed_count":1,"reason_count":1,"violation_row_count":2}}
614	  ```
615	
616	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
617	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry has
618	  exactly `version`, `verdict`, `reason_count` and `violation_row_count` in
619	  that order. `verdict` is the current per-version gate verdict (one of
620	  `pass`, `undetermined`, `fail`) under exactly the same computation as the
621	  per-version gate read; `reason_count` is the number of reasons currently
622	  lowering that verdict (the length of the per-version gate's reason list);
623	  `violation_row_count` is the violation row count of the latest recorded
624	  evaluation and is `null` — never omitted — when the version was never
625	  evaluated. `totals` has exactly `version_count`, `failed_count`,
626	  `reason_count` and `violation_row_count`: the number of version entries,
627	  the number of versions whose verdict is `fail`, and the sums of the
628	  per-version reason and violation row counts (null violation row counts
629	  count as zero).
630	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/quality-rule-coverage` — read-only cross-version
631	  check of how the dataset's schema fields are covered by quality rules,
632	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or
633	  deleted, and no rule definition or evaluation record is touched). The path
634	  carries only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no query
635	  parameters — any body bytes, including a purely whitespace or single-space
636	  body, or any query parameter → `422`; an unknown dataset → `404`, checked
637	  before the request shape, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
638	  compliance exports. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an
639	  empty `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
640	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
641	  trailing newline; the same data renders byte-identically after a process
642	  restart and ordering never depends on the database's natural order):
643	
644	  ```json
645	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"fields":[{"field":"amount","coverage":"disabled","kinds":["numeric_range"],"rule_ids":[3]},{"field":"id","coverage":"enabled","kinds":["not_null","unique"],"rule_ids":[1,2]},{"field":"region","coverage":"unregistered","kinds":null,"rule_ids":null}]}],"totals":{"version_count":1,"field_count":3,"enabled_count":1,"disabled_count":1,"unregistered_count":1}}
646	  ```
647	
648	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
649	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry has
650	  exactly `version` and `fields`, with every field of the version listed by
651	  field name ascending. Each field entry has exactly `field`, `coverage`,
652	  `kinds` and `rule_ids` in that order. `coverage` is one of the literals
653	  `enabled` (at least one enabled rule references the field), `disabled`
654	  (rules reference the field but all of them are disabled) and
655	  `unregistered` (no rule references the field). `kinds` is the
656	  de-duplicated list of referencing rule kinds sorted by literal value and
657	  `rule_ids` the referencing rules' ids de-duplicated and sorted ascending;
658	  every field of a unique rule counts as referenced. When a field is also
659	  referenced by disabled rules alongside enabled ones, their kinds and ids
660	  are included too. For an `unregistered` field both `kinds` and `rule_ids`
661	  are `null` — the keys are never omitted. `totals` has exactly
662	  `version_count`, `field_count`, `enabled_count`, `disabled_count` and
663	  `unregistered_count`: each is the sum of the per-version entries, and the
664	  field count equals the sum of the three per-state counts.

666	### Privacy policies
667	
668	Privacy policies attach a sensitivity classification and masking strategy to a
669	single field of a schema version, enabling role-based de-identification of row
670	data. Policies (including their enabled state) are persisted across restarts.
671	
672	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — register a
673	  policy. Body:
674	  `{"field": "email", "classification": "PII", "masking": "partial", "allowed_roles": ["analyst"]}`.
675	  `field` must name an existing field of the version; `classification` is a
676	  non-empty string; `masking` is `redact` or `partial`; `allowed_roles` is an
677	  array of distinct, non-empty role names and may be empty. Returns `201` with
678	  the submitted fields plus `id`, `enabled` (defaults to `true`) and
679	  `created_at`. Registering two policies for the same field within one version
680	  returns `409`. Unknown dataset/version/field → `404`; other invalid input →
681	  `422` and nothing is written.
682	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — list policies
683	  sorted by `id` ascending.
684	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/{policy_id}` —
685	  enable or disable a policy. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
686	  the updated policy. Unknown policy/dataset/version → `404`.
687	- `PUT /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/{policy_id}` —
688	  revise a policy. Body carries exactly the three adjustable fields:
689	  `{"classification": "PII", "masking": "partial", "allowed_roles":
690	  ["analyst"]}`, using the same value rules as registration — a non-empty
691	  `classification` after trimming, `masking` of `redact` or `partial`, and an
692	  `allowed_roles` array of distinct, non-empty-after-trimming role names that
693	  may be empty. The three fields are replaced together from one whole
694	  submission. The revision never changes the policy id, the field it belongs
695	  to, its `enabled` state or its `created_at`; it writes only the policy
696	  itself — no policy is created, no identification record is touched and no
697	  masking suggestion is registered. Returns `200` with the updated policy in
698	  the same shape as the policy read, and the revision survives restarts. The
699	  next privacy view read (and every later masked read) judges each value by
700	  the revised classification, masking and allowed roles. Already-written
701	  masking-hit records, access records and cleanup requests are unaffected —
702	  their contents and ordering stay as written; the grouping of the summary,
703	  diff and reconciliation responses keeps the same counting rules, while the
704	  policy classification and masking reported on trend rows (and the policy
705	  entries of the coverage check and compliance export) reflect the current
706	  values. Advisory masking suggestions are unaffected. Unknown
707	  dataset/version/policy → `404`, judged before every request-shape check;
708	  missing or extra fields, a blank `classification`, an illegal `masking`
709	  value, duplicate or blank `allowed_roles` entries, an empty or
710	  whitespace-only body, malformed JSON, a non-object payload or any query
711	  parameter → `422` and nothing is written. Concurrent revisions of the same
712	  policy have exactly one winner; the loser receives `409` and changes no
713	  field.
714	
715	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view` — return a
716	  role-scoped, order-preserving copy of submitted rows. Body:
717	  `{"role": "guest", "rows": [{...}, ...]}` with a non-empty `role` and a list
718	  of row objects. Response: `{"dataset", "version", "rows"}`. Only enabled
719	  policies whose field appears in a row mask the value when `role` is not in
720	  `allowed_roles`:
721	  - `redact` replaces every non-`null` value with `"***"`.
722	  - `partial` keeps the first character and last two characters of strings
723	    longer than 4 characters (e.g. `"alice@example.com"` → `"aom"`); every other
724	    non-`null` value (short strings, numbers, booleans, …) is replaced with
725	    `"***"`.
726	  - `null` values and fields without a policy are returned unchanged; rows
727	    missing a covered field are left without it.
728	
729	  Every successful view also appends one audit record per value it actually
730	  masked (the same field masked in several rows yields one record per masked
731	  value; a role in `allowed_roles`, a `null` value, an uncovered field or a
732	  disabled policy never hits); the records are persisted per version and are
733	  append-only.
734	
735	  Every successful view additionally appends exactly one access record,
736	  whether or not it masked any value (an empty `rows` submission is recorded
737	  too). Rejected or failed views leave neither kind of record.
738	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/access-records`
739	  — list every access record of the version, ordered by `sequence` ascending
740	  (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has `sequence`,
741	  `role`, `row_count` (the number of submitted rows), `masked_count` (the
742	  number of masking-hit records the same view wrote, so the two logs
743	  cross-check) and `created_at`. The endpoint takes no request body and no
744	  query parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is
745	  written.
746	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records`
747	  — list every masking-hit record of the version, ordered by `sequence`
748	  ascending (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has
749	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`. The
750	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
751	  dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is written.
752	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/search`
753	  — read-only filtered retrieval of the same masking-hit records. The
754	  response is the same record collection as the full list (each record has
755	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`),
756	  sorted by `sequence` ascending; a filter that matches nothing returns an
757	  empty array, never an error. All filters are optional query parameters and
758	  combine with AND:
759	  - `role` — exact match against the requesting role recorded on the hit,
760	    case-insensitive (no substring or other fuzzy matching).
761	  - `field` — exact match against the hit field name, case-insensitive.
762	  - `start` / `end` — closed write-time interval: a record matches when its
763	    `created_at` is between the bounds inclusive. Each bound is a
764	    timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time (offset or `Z`); either bound may be
765	    given alone. `start` later than `end` → `422`.
766	
767	  The endpoint takes no request body; an unparseable or timezone-less
768	  `start`/`end`, or any query parameter other than `role`, `field`, `start`
769	  and `end`, → `422`. Unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
770	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list. It is strictly read-only:
771	  no record is written, modified or deleted and the summary/diff responses
772	  are unaffected.
773	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/summary`
774	  — read-only compliance summary computed fresh from the persisted records on
775	  every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted). Response:
776	  `{"dataset", "version", "groups"}`; `groups` is an empty array when the
777	  version has no records. Each group merges records with the same `field`,
778	  `policy_id`, `role` and `masking` (different roles or masking modes stay
779	  separate) and lists `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking`, `hit_count`
780	  (one record counts as one hit), `first_hit_at` and `last_hit_at` (the
781	  earliest and latest record `created_at` in the group). Groups sort by
782	  `field`, then `policy_id`, `role` and `masking`, all ascending. The
783	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
784	  dataset/version → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
785	  record list.
786	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/trend`
787	  — read-only hit trend aggregated by privacy policy, computed fresh from the
788	  persisted records on every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted).
789	  Hits of the same policy merge across roles (a disabled policy's historical
790	  hits still count). Response: `{"dataset", "version", "policies", "totals"}`;
791	  `policies` is an empty array when the version has no records. Each policy
792	  row carries `policy_id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `total_hits`
793	  and `days`; policies sort by `policy_id` ascending. `days` lists only UTC
794	  calendar days with hits (a write time with a non-zero offset buckets by its
795	  UTC day), sorted ascending with no zero-filled gaps; each entry has `day`
796	  (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `hit_count` (one record counts once), `hit_count_delta`
797	  (difference from the previous listed day, `null` on the first) and `trend`
798	  (`up`/`down`/`flat`, or `none` on the first day). `totals` gives
799	  `total_hits` (the sum of the row totals), `policy_count` (policies with
800	  hits) and `day_count` (distinct hit days over the whole version, the
801	  per-policy day union). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
802	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
803	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list.
804	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests`
805	  — open a two-stage retention cleanup request for the version's masking-hit
806	  records. Body contains exactly `reason` and `before`:
807	  `{"reason": "legal hold expired", "before": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`.
808	  `reason` must be a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace;
809	  `before` must be an ISO-8601 date-time carrying a timezone (offset or `Z`),
810	  and a record belongs to the target set only when its hit write time is
811	  strictly earlier than that instant. Creating a request only returns a
812	  preview — no hit record is deleted or modified, and the record list,
813	  search, summary, diff, reconcile and trend responses stay unchanged.
814	  Returns `201` with `id`, `reason` (trimmed), `before` (echoed as
815	  submitted), `status` (`pending`), `created_at` and a `preview` block:
816	  `hit_count` (the number of records that would be cleaned up),
817	  `first_hit_at` / `last_hit_at` (the earliest and latest hit times in the
818	  target set, `null` when the set is empty) and `fields` (the distinct field
819	  names involved, sorted ascending; `[]` when empty). The target set is
820	  fixed at creation time: masking-hit records written afterwards never enter
821	  the request even when they precede the cutoff by clock time. At most one
822	  pending request may exist per version; creating another while one is open
823	  returns `409` and writes nothing (confirmed requests never block a new
824	  one). Unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing/non-string/blank `reason`,
825	  missing/unparseable/timezone-less `before`, an extra body field, a
826	  non-JSON/non-object body or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
827	  written, with 404 taking precedence.
828	- `GET .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests` — list the
829	  version's cleanup requests sorted by request `id` ascending (empty when
830	  there are none). Confirmed requests stay listed and requests survive
831	  process restarts. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
832	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
833	- `POST .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests/{request_id}/confirm`
834	  — confirm a request with an empty request body and no query parameters.
835	  Confirmation atomically deletes exactly the target set frozen at creation
836	  and sets `status` to `confirmed`; the response is the request plus
837	  `confirmed_at` and `deleted_count` (the number of records actually
838	  deleted, possibly zero). Confirming an already-confirmed request returns
839	  `409` and never changes data again; concurrent confirmations have exactly
840	  one winner (the others get `409`) and can never leave the records half
841	  deleted. After a cleanup the surviving hit records keep their original
842	  `sequence` numbers and later hits continue the existing increasing run
843	  without reusing cleaned numbers; the record list and search return only
844	  surviving records, and summary, trend, diff and reconcile recompute from
845	  them. Access records are not cleaned up and the processing-task audit
846	  chain remains immutable. A request body or query parameter on the confirm
847	  endpoint → `422`; unknown dataset/version/request → `404` (precedence
848	  matches the hit-record reads), and confirming a confirmed request →
849	  `409`.
850	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-compliance-export` — read-only
851	  cross-version export of the dataset's whole privacy compliance state,
852	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or
853	  deleted, and no hit record, access record or cleanup request is touched).
854	  The path carries only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no
855	  query parameters (`422`); an unknown dataset → `404`, with the same
856	  404-before-422 precedence as the hit-record reads. A dataset without
857	  schema versions returns `200` with an empty `versions` array and all-zero
858	  totals, never an error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
859	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
860	
861	  ```json
862	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"policies":[...],"hit_count":0,"masked_count":1,"view_count":2,"cleanup_requests":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
863	  ```
864	
865	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
866	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
867	  has exactly `version`, `policies`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
868	  `view_count`, `cleanup_requests` in that order. `policies` lists the
869	  version's registered policies ordered by policy id; each policy has `id`,
870	  `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `allowed_roles` and `enabled`.
871	  `cleanup_requests` lists the version's cleanup requests ordered by request
872	  id (both pending and confirmed are retained); each has `id`, `reason`,
873	  `status` and `created_at`. `hit_count` is the number of masking-hit
874	  records currently stored for the version, `masked_count` is the sum of the
875	  access records' masked-value counts and `view_count` is the number of
876	  access records; all three reflect the records surviving a confirmed
877	  cleanup. `totals` has exactly `policy_count`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
878	  `view_count` and `cleanup_request_count`, each the sum of the per-version
879	  values over the whole dataset.
880	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-policy-coverage` — read-only cross-version
881	  check of the dataset's privacy policy coverage, computed fresh on every
882	  read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or deleted, and no policy
883	  or identification record is touched). The path carries only the dataset
884	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters (`422`); an
885	  unknown dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
886	  compliance export. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an
887	  empty `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
888	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly
889	  one trailing newline):
890	
891	  ```json
892	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"fields":[...],"candidates":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
893	  ```
894	
895	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
896	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
897	  has exactly `version`, `fields`, `candidates` in that order. `fields`
898	  lists every field of the version ordered by field name; each entry has
899	  `field`, `coverage`, `classification`, `masking` and `enabled`, where
900	  `coverage` is `enabled` (an enabled policy is registered), `disabled` (a
901	  policy is registered but disabled) or `unregistered` (no policy), and the
902	  last three keys report the registered policy's classification, masking and
903	  enabled state (all `null` when no policy is registered). `candidates`
904	  lists the advisory suggestions for fields that were identified with at
905	  least one name or sample hit but carry no privacy policy yet, ordered by
906	  identification record id ascending; each candidate has exactly `field`,
907	  `classification` and `masking`, and an identified field whose name and
908	  samples both missed does not appear. The candidates are a compliance
909	  self-check reference only: they never register a policy and never rewrite
910	  an identification record. `totals` has exactly `version_count`,
911	  `field_count`, `enabled_count`, `disabled_count`, `unregistered_count`
912	  and `candidate_count`, each the sum of the per-version values over the
913	  whole dataset.
914	
915	### Sensitive-field identification
916	
917	Sensitive-field identification produces candidate annotations for the fields of
918	a schema version. It complements the manual privacy policies but never creates
919	or modifies one: an identification is advisory only. Records (including their
920	stable ids) persist across restarts.
921	
922	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
923	  identify one field. The body contains exactly `field` and `samples`:
924	  `{"field": "contact_email", "samples": ["alice@example.com"]}`. `field` must
925	  name an existing field of the version; its name and type are taken from the
926	  version definition. `samples` is an array of JSON scalars (strings, numbers,
927	  booleans or `null`) and may be empty; objects or arrays reject the whole
928	  request. The samples are never stored or echoed back. Returns the record;
929	  the first submission for a field returns `201`, re-running the same field
930	  refreshes the record in place (the id is unchanged) and returns `200`.
931	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
932	  return every identification record of the version sorted by id ascending
933	  (empty when there are none). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
934	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
935	
936	  Each record has `id`, `field`, `field_type`, `evidence`, `confidence`,
937	  `source` and `created_at`. `source` references the identified field as
938	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. `evidence` is the ordered, de-duplicated
939	  list of hit kinds, name hits before sample hits:
940	
941	  - **Name hits** — the field name contains a sensitive word case-insensitively
942	    as a substring. The words are `email`, `phone`, `id_card`, `password`,
943	    `token` and `birth`, emitting `name:<word>` in that order.
944	  - **Sample hits** — only string sample values are inspected (numbers,
945	    booleans and `null` never hit), and only when the field's declared type is
946	    `string`; a field declared with any other type is matched by name alone,
947	    even when a sample looks like an email. `sample:email` requires exactly
948	    one `@` with non-empty text on both sides and a dot in the domain;
949	    `sample:phone` requires an 11-digit string starting with `1`. Either format
950	    matching is sufficient.
951	
952	  `confidence` is `high` when both the name and the samples hit, `medium` for
953	  samples only, `low` for the name only and `none` when neither side hits
954	  (`evidence` is then an empty list but the record is still generated).
955	
956	  One record is kept per field: a re-run overwrites the evidence and confidence
957	  in place with a stable id. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; a field that does
958	  not exist in the version → `404`; missing or extra body fields, a
959	  non-string or blank field name, a `samples` value that is not an array of
960	  scalars (objects and arrays included), an empty body, malformed JSON or any
961	  query parameter → `422` and nothing is written.
962	
963	#### Masking strategy suggestions
964	
965	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions`
966	  — read-only advisory masking-strategy candidates derived from the version's
967	  identification records. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
968	  parameters (`422` if either is present, with nothing written); unknown
969	  dataset/version → `404`. A version without identification records returns an
970	  empty list rather than an error.
971	
972	  Each candidate has exactly `field`, `classification`, `masking` and
973	  `allowed_roles`. Only records whose name or samples hit produce a candidate;
974	  a record with empty evidence is omitted. Candidates follow the identification
975	  records' `id` ascending and are recomputed on every read, so refreshing an
976	  identification changes the suggestion on the next request. The endpoint
977	  writes nothing, never registers a privacy policy and leaves the
978	  identification records' fields, ordering and refresh semantics untouched;
979	  the privacy view continues to mask according to registered policies only.
980	
981	  - `classification` is `PII` for email, phone, id-card and birthday hits, and
982	    `CREDENTIAL` for password and token hits. A field hitting both is `PII`.
983	  - `masking` reuses the privacy-view vocabulary: `partial` for `PII`
984	    candidates and `redact` for `CREDENTIAL` candidates (a both-kinds field
985	    takes `partial`); no new masking format is introduced.
986	  - `allowed_roles` is always an empty list: the suggested masking applies to
987	    every role, granting none an unmasked view.
988	
989	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions/register`
990	  — turn the current advisory candidates into registered privacy policies. The
991	  body contains only `{"fields": ["<field>", ...]}`: a non-empty array of
992	  distinct field names, each non-empty after trimming and naming an existing
993	  field of the version that currently has a masking suggestion candidate.
994	  Returns `201` with one privacy policy record per requested field, in the
995	  request's field-name order; each record has the same fields as the manual
996	  policy creation response (`id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`,
997	  `allowed_roles`, `enabled`, `created_at`), is enabled by default and gets a
998	  service-generated id and timestamp. Each policy copies its candidate's
999	  `classification` and `masking` verbatim with the candidate's empty
1000	  `allowed_roles`, so after registration every role sees those fields masked;
1001	  the next privacy view read masks according to the new policies. The whole
1002	  batch is validated before anything is written, so any rejection writes no
1003	  policy and no timestamp. Unknown dataset/version, or a named field that does
1004	  not exist in the version → `404`; a field without an available candidate
1005	  (never identified, or whose identification record currently yields no
1006	  candidate) or one that already has a privacy policy → `409`; two concurrent
1007	  registrations of the same field leave exactly one winner. Missing or extra
1008	  body fields, an empty `fields` array, duplicate, non-string or blank names,
1009	  an empty body, a whitespace-only body, malformed JSON or any query parameter
1010	  → `422` and nothing is written. Registration only reads the identification
1011	  records and field definitions; it never writes or auto-refreshes an
1012	  identification, and the read-only suggestions endpoint stays unchanged.
1013	
1014	### Row snapshots
1015	
1016	A row snapshot persistently records the rows of a schema version at one point in
1017	time. Snapshots (including their rows) survive restarts.
1018	
1019	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — persist a snapshot.
1020	  Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}` where `rows` must be an array of JSON objects
1021	  (it may be empty). The JSON values and the order of rows/object keys are deep
1022	  copied verbatim. A SHA-256 content fingerprint of the saved row sequence is
1023	  computed at creation and written together with the rows in one atomic write,
1024	  so it can later attest that the persisted rows are unchanged; the fingerprint
1025	  is not part of the response, which stays `id`, `dataset`, `version`,
1026	  `created_at` and `row_count` (no rows). In the same transaction the service
1027	  also maintains the snapshot diff cache incrementally (see "Snapshot diff
1028	  cache" below): the canonical form of every row (key-sorted compact JSON text
1029	  in stored row order) and the sorted set of top-level field names are written
1030	  together with the snapshot, and one `created` record is appended to the
1031	  version's cache trail. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; malformed or
1032	  non-object rows → `422` and nothing is written.
1033	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — list snapshot
1034	  metadata sorted by `id` ascending (no `rows`).
1035	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}` — return
1036	  the metadata together with the saved `rows`. Unknown dataset/version/snapshot
1037	  → `404`.
1038	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/verify` —
1039	  read-only content-fingerprint verification, appended one segment after the
1040	  single-snapshot read address and accepting GET only. On every read the
1041	  fingerprint of the currently persisted row sequence is recomputed and
1042	  compared with the fingerprint stored with the snapshot at creation; the
1043	  snapshot and its rows are only read, never written or modified. The JSON
1044	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, lowercase
1045	  booleans, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`,
1046	  `version`, `snapshot_id`, `row_count`, `stored_hash`, `computed_hash` and
1047	  `valid` in that order. `stored_hash` is the fingerprint written at creation,
1048	  `computed_hash` the freshly recomputed one and `valid` is `true` exactly
1049	  while both agree; directly changing, adding, deleting or replacing a saved
1050	  row makes them differ and changes `computed_hash`. Both verdicts return
1051	  `200`. The fingerprint hashes the saved row sequence as a JSON array in row
